text: In Tableau Desktop, publishing means pushing a workbook up to a server. Tableau Next works differently. There is no publish button in that sense, because your assets already live in a workspace on the Salesforce platform. What you decide is who can see them, and where they show up.

The workspace is the unit of collaboration. This is a real Tableau Next workspace, holding a dashboard, visualizations, semantic models, and tables. You can share individual assets or the whole workspace, and referenced or extended assets carry their own badges.

There are three main ways to put work in front of people. Share it, by adding users or groups. Embed it, by dropping the Tableau Next dashboard component onto a Lightning page, with filters tied to the record. Or generate a template, so other teams can install and customize it. As of this writing, sharing into Slack is also supported. Check current release notes.

Know the access model. Workspaces take a viewer or editor role. Dashboards, visualizations, and semantic models are shared as viewer. General access starts out restricted. And the trap: sharing a workspace does not share the underlying data. Data access is governed separately in Data 360, so plan both layers together.
So nothing is published in the Desktop sense. You share, embed, or template, and you always check the data permissions. Next up: choosing between Tableau Next and Tableau Desktop.
